title: Coasters and pendulums
target: Use height differences to predict speed in ideal motion.
criteria: Identify the relevant vertical height change.
Separate path length from gravitational energy change.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A coaster descends from elevation 9 m to 4 m along a 12 m track. What height change belongs in mgΔh?
cpa.guide: Vertical change is 4 − 9 = −5 m, independent of track length.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A pendulum bob is 0.3 m above its lowest position at release. Its string is 1.2 m long. Which value is the initial height relative to the bottom?
cpa.guide: Use the vertical height above the chosen reference, not string length.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 3 kg coaster model descends 2 m without resistance. Use g = 10 N/kg. What is its kinetic-energy gain?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A pendulum starts with 18 J of potential energy and no kinetic energy. At one point it has 7 J of potential energy. With no losses, what is K there?
cpa.guide: Conserved total is 18 J; K = 18 − 7 = 11 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two frictionless coaster tracks connect identical start and end heights. A cart starts with the same speed on each. Which statement follows?
options: Equal final speed proves equal travel time.
Final speeds are equal, although travel times can differ.
The flatter track must end at zero speed.
Longer track always gives greater final speed.
cpa.guide: Energy fixes final speed from the endpoints; the path can affect timing.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A longer real coaster track gives a lower final speed than a shorter one with the same drop. Which explanation is plausible?
options: More energy may have transferred to internal energy through resistance.
The longer path necessarily reduced the cart’s mass.
Height no longer affects gravitational energy.
cpa.guide: Real resistive work depends on the path and can reduce final kinetic energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
